title: Temporal agent-server launch activity timeouts must exceed sandbox readiness budget
answers: How long should start_to_close_timeout be for agent-server Temporal launch activities?
Why did Temporal time out during await_agent_server_ready or start_agent_server?
What is the maximum allowed wait time for sandbox health checks during task startup?
body:
Temporal activities waiting on agent-server startup must configure a start_to_close_timeout (15 minutes) greater than the maximum sandbox health check budget (products/tasks/backend/logic/services/sandbox.py:SETUP_HOOKS_BUDGET_SECONDS).
Enforced in products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/workflow.py:_start_agent_server and products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/workflow.py:_await_agent_server_ready.
If skipped, Temporal aborts the activity while the sandbox is still legitimately waiting for SessionStart hooks, causing false startup errors and conflicting sandbox retries.
applies: Temporal workflows orchestrating agent-server startup and sandbox readiness
says: Background task runner aborts while workspace environment is still running setup scripts
Cloud agent execution fails with workflow timeout on projects with heavy dependencies
Allow background workers longer wait times before aborting slow repository startup tasks
Initial workspace setup triggers premature failure notifications instead of waiting for completion
